properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-16, in his words: *"my other brother (Seth) is trying to build some houses in Seattle, WA. He is going to send me some architectural drawings for what has been developed. He was telling me an architect costs $250 per hour and they often make mistakes — then he has to bring the drawings back through the Seattle city planners to get approved and to get permits, etc. I'd like to set this up as a test case where we actually start from genesis and design some apartments/condos that meets all of Seattle building codes, etc."*

THE SITUATION, as relayed: an architect's drawings already exist and are on their way; the pain is the cost of each mistake — hours at $250 and another round through the city planners. Seth is the source of the situation; the test-case idea is Anthony's. Seth is not recorded as a Contributor here; he would be, in his own words, on the project's own graph.

═══ WHAT THE GRAPH ALREADY HOLDS, checked before writing ═══
· dec:idea-who-authors-the-domain-artifact (2026-08-30, revisited today): the ring, the garage, the biodome — and the reframing that the agent may author the REVIEWABLE SOURCE, never the opaque output; and bhome's plan sheet measured today as the direct-drawing case that record warned against.
· req:the-agent-never-authors-what-requires-accountable-sign-off (ACCEPTED): a permit submission is exactly the artifact the agent must not sign.
· EnvironmentRule already carries rule_type `building_code` and `zoning`, with COMPLIES_WITH and VIOLATES edges and a compliance gap — the vocabulary for "meets Seattle codes" exists and has one recorded use.
· ingest-corpus: the skill for a FOLDER of documents, which is what two titles of the Seattle Municipal Code are.
· dec:nested-graphs: a design is its own graph when separately owned — this is Seth's project, so its design lives in its own repository and store, not in reflow2's; only the trial-as-evidence about reflow2 belongs here.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══
A. GENESIS FROM SCRATCH — start an empty design from a brief (units, site, budget), capture Seattle's codes as EnvironmentRules, design the building as requirements/interfaces/allocations, and have the agent author a parametric BIM source (FreeCAD BIM workbench script or Blender's Bonsai add-on → IFC → PDF sheets). The test he asked for literally. ⚠️ Cost: the largest option, and it measures two things at once (can reflow2 hold a building design? can an agent author BIM source?) so a failure is hard to attribute; and it produces drawings an architect must then redo under their own stamp, which may cost more than it saves.
B. ADOPT WHAT EXISTS AND CHECK IT — Seth sends the architect's drawings; register them as Artifacts, recover the intent (adopt skill), capture the codes as rules, and run the compliance checks as Verifications by analysis. The deliverable is a list of what the drawings miss BEFORE the city says so. ⭐ Cheapest, matches what is actually about to happen (drawings are coming), and it measures the one thing that pays — mistakes caught upstream of $250/hour — without the agent holding any pen. ⚠️ Cost: reading a PDF plan set into the design is manual (reflow2 does no file I/O and no drawing parsing); the codes are a large ingest; and "meets all of Seattle building codes" is a claim nobody can make from a plan set alone — structural, energy and fire reviews each want their own analysis.
C. B FIRST, THEN A FOR ONE ALTERNATIVE — check the architect's set, then design ONE alternative unit or floor as a parametric source to see whether the agent's output is something the architect would accept as a starting point. Attributable, incremental, and it turns the who-authors question into a measurement on a real case. ⚠️ Cost: two projects' worth of set-up before either answer arrives.
D. DECLINE THE DRAWING HALF ENTIRELY — reflow2 holds the requirements, the code rules and the verification matrix; the architect holds every drawing; the test case is only whether the checklist catches what the planners would. ⚠️ Cost: answers the money question and none of his "which tool" question.

═══ THE TOOL QUESTION, answered as far as the domain allows ═══
Not .stl, and not Blender bare. For buildings the accepted interchange is IFC; the open tools that write it are FreeCAD (BIM workbench, Python-scriptable — the parametric, diffable source the reframing wants) and Blender only through the Bonsai add-on. What Seattle's permit office reviews is a PDF plan set, stamped by a licensed architect for multifamily. So whichever option is chosen, the shape is: reflow2 holds intent, rules and checks → the agent may author a reviewable script or schedule → an open tool compiles it → the architect owns and stamps the set. The ring is the same shape with OpenSCAD/CadQuery → .stl and no stamp.

═══ THE TEST THAT WOULD DECIDE IT ═══
Take the drawings Seth sends. Count the findings reflow2 raises against the captured Seattle rules, then count how many of those the city planners raise on the next round. If the first list contains the second, option B alone pays for itself and A is a luxury; if it misses most of them, the codes were not captured well enough for any option to matter yet.

📌 NOT INTENT YET, his own framing: "I'd like to set this up as a test case." The project's design starts on its own graph the day Seth's drawings arrive; this node records why the trial is worth running and which shape it should take.
properties.name: OPEN — Seth's houses in Seattle as the field trial for designing something that is not software: genesis a code-compliant apartment/condo design, or adopt the architect's drawings and check them, and which tool holds the pen?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill, nothing promoted. Kept separate from the who-authors idea because that one asks a general question about who holds the pen, and this one asks whether a specific real project should be the measurement that answers it — and the answer to the second can be yes even if the first stays open. The counter-argument to his literal ask (genesis from scratch measures two things at once and produces drawings the architect must redo) is recorded beside it rather than argued in conversation. The tool question is answered as far as the domain's facts allow rather than left as a preference, because "IFC via FreeCAD or Bonsai, PDF for the city, stamped by the architect" is not an opinion.
